note: Types a ratification batch considered and did not admit. PROPOSE reads this as a veto set so it never re-proposes a type already ruled out by name. Recovered from the 'Rejected, and deliberately absent from this table' prose in the per-cohort identity and admission fragments that issue #96 deleted (readable at d40d9f5ded^) and from live/e2e/estates/remainder/README.md; recovered_from names the source each type came from. THE INVARIANT: this set and internal/live/identity.DefaultTable are disjoint. A type that is admitted must not be vetoed, because two contradictory rulings are not conservatism. TestRejectedLedgerIsDisjointFromAdmitted enforces it. Issue #131 rebuilt the ledger against that invariant: the first recovery harvested every type name adjacent to the word Rejected rather than the subject of each '- <type>:' bullet, which admitted 58 types into the veto set and lost 5 genuine rejections. Over-inclusion is safe only among types nobody admitted; among admitted types it is a defect. A blocked_on field names the issue an entry is waiting on, where one has been identified; loadRejectedTypes reads only the key set, so the field is for a human tracing why a type is still here. Fourteen entries carry blocked_on #233 as of 2026-08-16: untaggable types whose identity carries a server-minted segment beside a config-supplied one, where the refusal is not about vocabulary the table lacks (it carries 51 such rows) but about having nowhere to write an ownership marker.

The actual blocker is SERVER-ASSIGNED IDENTITY WITH NO MARKER-CAPABLE ARGUMENT, BLOCKED ON #233. live/survey-full.json records signals.taggable=false for this type at v6.59.0, so admitting it would put every instance in NeedsDiscovery, make stamp.go:743's mustStamp true, and raise an unconditional unstampable fatal at stamp.go:537 - and live-mv's locateByList (mv.go:673) would match on a tofu-address tag that cannot exist, reporting "No live resource carries estate X and address Y" about an account it never checked. That is strictly worse than today's refusal, which is why this stays. EVIDENCE FOR THE SHAPE, recomputed from committed artifacts rather than quoted: live/import-grammar.json's own per-segment attribution for this type labels "membership_id" from the doc's Attribute Reference and "identity_store_id" from its Argument Reference. The four taggable members of the same bucket (aws_ecs_task_set, aws_eks_pod_identity_association, aws_prometheus_anomaly_detector, aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace) were admitted in the same batch, because for them the ownership marker is the discriminator and the parent scope only narrows the candidate set: parent-scoped enumeration can CONFIRM an identity the configuration has already narrowed to one, it cannot SUPPLY one.

aws_quicksight_folder.reason: row-gen -propose offered this as its sole proposed:server-assigned candidate (issue #245's server-assigned slice), rule class 'the Import section's own prose names a segment that is an exported attribute, not a configuration argument' at a reported 16/16 historical match - but the 17th instance fails the spot-check contract's own step 1. The provider's aws_quicksight_folder.html.markdown Argument Reference lists folder_id as (Required, Forces new resource): a client-supplied argument, not a computed attribute; aws_account_id is likewise a real (Optional) argument that defaults to the provider's own account. Both segments of the import ID ("AWS account ID and folder ID name separated by a comma") are configuration-derived, not server-minted. The registry evidence agrees and was overridden incorrectly: primary_identifier=[AwsAccountId, FolderId], both in create_only_properties, NEITHER in read_only_properties - the exact shape of all nine other CFN-modeled aws_quicksight_* types (analysis, custom_permissions, dashboard, data_set, data_source, refresh_schedule, template, theme, vpc_connection), every one of which row-gen correctly buckets 'needs hand separator' rather than server-assigned. The classifier's note ('attribute[s] folder ID name to the Attribute Reference, not the Argument Reference') is factually wrong: folder_id is in the Argument Reference. This is a live bug in the import-grammar-precedence rule (tools/row-gen/importprecedence.go) that fires on the computed `id` attribute's prose description ('A comma-delimited string joining AWS account ID and folder ID') without checking whether the named segment is independently a real argument elsewhere in the doc. Left unadmitted; the rule itself needs a fix in a separate slot, not a per-type override here. See issue #245.
